notes: NYC Fair Workweek Law, retail (Admin. Code Title 20 ch. 12): covers businesses with 20+ employees primarily selling consumer goods at stores in NYC. Effective Nov. 26, 2017.

Retail rules are prohibitions, not premiums: schedules 72 h ahead; no on-call shifts; no cancel/cut of >15 min within 72 h (exceptions); added time within 72 h only with written consent. Encoded as change_premium_hours=0 with extra key changes_restricted_within_notice=true.
Violation of the 72-hour schedule notice may cost $300 per affected worker (DCWP FAQ).
No retail rest-between-shifts rule (NYC's clopening rule applies to fast food, out of scope).
Minimum wage effective date not stated on the source page; rate confirmed in effect as of last_verified (page says it stays the same on Jan 1, 2027).

rules.summary: NYC retail employers with 20+ employees must give schedules 72 hours ahead and may not use on-call shifts or cancel or add shifts within 72 hours without consent.

citation.title: NYC DCWP — Fair Workweek Law in Retail: FAQ
citation.excerpt: Retail employers must both post at the workplace AND provide workers with a written work schedule at least 72 hours before the first shift

rules.summary: The minimum wage in New York City is $17.00 an hour.

citation.title: NY Department of Labor — Minimum Wage
citation.excerpt: $17.00 per hour in New York City, Long Island, and Westchester County (stays the same on January 1, 2027)
